FIRE INCIDENT - MOUNT PEARL
(Nov 27th)
~ 12:45 p.m; Emergency crews have responded to, and are currently on the scene of a reported electrical fire at a group of commercial businesses on Merchant Drive in Mount Pearl.
The businesses are currently evacuated.
More info soon. ￼

RCMP INVESTIGATING SUSPICIOUS FIRE THAT DESTROYED VACANT HOME
(Nov 27th)
Bay St. George RCMP is investigating a suspicious fire that destroyed a vacant residential property in Stephenville Crossing overnight.
Shortly before 12:30 a.m. on November 27, officers with the Bay St. George RCMP detachment and members of the Stephenville Crossing Volunteer Fire Department responded to a reported fire at a vacant home on Water Street.
No one was inside the residence at the time. However, the building was destroyed by the fire before it was extinguished.
Police say a witness reported seeing an unknown male leaving the area on foot around the time the fire was discovered. The witness was unable to provide a detailed description of the individual.
Investigators are asking anyone with information about the fire, or anyone with surveillance camera or dashcam footage from the Water Street area between 12:00 a.m. and 1:00 a.m. on November 27, to contact Bay St. George RCMP at 709-643-2118.
Anyone wishing to provide information anonymously can contact Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).

COLLISION - PRINCE PHILIP DRIVE
(Nov 27th)
~ 9:00 a.m; Emergency crews are on the scene of a three-vehicle rear-end collision on Prince Philip Drive heading eastbound nearing the intersection to Wicklow Street in St. John’s. There are no injuries to reported.
Traffic remains slowed and down to one lane of travel.

MAN CHARGED AFTER EXPLOSIVES CLAIM AT ST. JOHN’S AIRPORT
(Nov 27th)
On Thursday evening (Nov 26th), At approximately 6:40 p.m; Officers with the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) Operational Patrol Services responded to St. John’s International Airport located at 100 World Parkway in St. John’s. 
Upon arrival, officers learned that a 39-year-old male had told airport staff he had a bag of explosives.
The male was arrested and charged under the Aeronautics Act with Interfering with the Operations of an Air Navigation Facility.
He was held to appear before a Judge.
No explosives were located, and police confirmed there was never any danger to the travelling public.

DRIVER CAUGHT TRAVELLING 164 KM/H ON TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY
(Nov 27th)
A 41-year-old woman had her vehicle seized and driver’s licence suspended after being caught travelling well above the posted speed limit on the Trans-Canada Highway Thursday night (Nov. 26).
A member of the Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) observed the vehicle travelling at 164 km/h in a posted 100 km/h zone.
As a result, the female driver was ticketed, her vehicle was seized, and her driver’s licence was suspended.

TWO PEOPLE ARRESTED FOLLOWING STRING OF THEFTS ON THE NORTHEAST AVALON
(Nov 26th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) has charged two people who were wanted in connection with a series of recent thefts on the Northeast Avalon, including a theft valued at approximately $13,000 from a St. John’s jewellery store.
On Wednesday, November 25, around 4:00 p.m., officers responded to a tip from the public and located wanted individuals Taylor Seigmiller, 28, and James Peach, 30, at a residence in Conception Bay South.
Both individuals were arrested on outstanding warrants for failing to comply with an appearance notice related to theft charges.
During the investigation, Seigmiller was also identified as being responsible for a theft on September 10 and a $13,000 theft from a St. John’s jewellery store on October 1. Previous attempts by police to locate her had been unsuccessful.
As a result, Seigmiller was additionally charged with theft over $5,000 and theft under $5,000.
Both individuals were held to appear in court.
The RNC continues to encourage anyone who witnesses suspicious activity to report it directly to police at 709-729-8000. Crimes in progress should be reported by calling 911.

RCMP CONTINUES SEARCH FOR WANTED FEMALE
(Nov 26th)
Burin Peninsula RCMP is renewing its request for assistance locating 51-year-old Jodi Lynn Lake. Lake is the subject of an arrest warrant and continues to actively evade police.
She is approximately 5’ 11” (180 cm) tall, and 145 lbs (66 kg) with brown hair and blue eyes. Police believe Lake may be in the St. John’s metro region or in the Burin area.
Lake is wanted for failing to attend court in connection Criminal Code charges including breaking and entering, theft and failing to comply with undertaking for the purpose of Identification of Criminals Act.
If you have information regarding the current location of Jodi Lake, please dial 911, contact police at 1-800-709-RCMP (7267) or call your local police detachment as soon as possible.

24-HOUR SNOW CLEARING TO EXPAND ACROSS ENTIRE TRANS-CANADA HIGHWAY
(Nov 26th)
The provincial government has announced plans to expand 24-hour snow clearing and ice control operations along the entire Trans-Canada Highway in Newfoundland, extending from St. John’s to Port aux Basques.
The proposed expansion would see more than 1,300 additional kilometres of highway receive round-the-clock winter maintenance.
The expansion will depend on the recruitment of additional highway maintenance operators.
The move would extend overnight and early-morning snow clearing and ice control coverage across the province’s main highway corridor, providing additional winter maintenance for motorists travelling during the winter months.

RNC REAFFIRMS COMMITMENT TO SUPPORT VICTIMS OF INTIMATE PARTNER VIOLENCE
(Nov 26th)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) is reaffirming its commitment to supporting victims and survivors of intimate partner violence, while continuing efforts to help end violence against women and girls.
The RNC says its Intimate Partner Violence Unit continues to provide support to individuals experiencing intimate partner violence and works alongside community partners to help break down barriers faced by victims of abuse.
Police say control and intimidation can create significant barriers for victims, and the RNC remains dedicated to connecting vulnerable individuals with resources and support services throughout the community.
The RNC is also encouraging anyone who suspects someone may be living in an abusive environment to reach out, noting that police are available to listen and help support victims and survivors.
Anyone experiencing violence at the hands of a partner is encouraged to contact the RNC’s Intimate Partner Violence Unit at 709-729-8093, when it is safe to do so.
The unit can also be reached at the same number for support and direction to available resources.

MAN ARRESTED FOR IMPAIRED DRIVING TWICE IN LESS THAN TWO HOURS AND ACCUSED OF BRIBING AN OFFICER
(Nov 26)
A 50-year-old man is facing multiple criminal charges after being arrested twice for impaired driving in Paradise on Wednesday afternoon.
At approximately 1:15 p.m. on November 25, RNC officers received a complaint of an impaired driver in the Topsail Road area of Paradise.
Officers located the man at a local bar, where he was arrested for impaired driving. Subsequent breathalyzer testing registered more than three times the legal limit.
Police impounded his vehicle, suspended his driver’s licence and charged him with impaired driving.
Less than two hours later, at approximately 3:11 p.m., officers returned to the man’s residence to inform him of an additional charge of bribery of a police officer.
Upon arrival, officers noticed the garage door was wide open and a Corvette was missing.
Police then observed the man driving past them in his Corvette. He was stopped and arrested for impaired driving for the second time that afternoon.
The man now faces multiple charges of impaired driving, operating a vehicle while over the legal limit, driving while suspended and bribery of a police officer.
The Corvette was also seized, and the man was transported to the city lockup, where he awaits an appearance before a judge.

MISSING 13 YEAR OLD - LABRADOR
(Nov 26th)
~ 11:35 a.m; Police in Sheshatshiu are asking for the public’s help locating 13-year-old Micah Michel.
He was last seen at the local youth centre on Wednesday, November 25 around 9:30 p.m, wearing a black hooded sweatshirt, black pants, black shoes and a Toronto Blue Jays hat.
Police are concerned for his well-being and would like to speak to him as soon as possible.
If you have information about his current location, please contact Sheshatshiu RCMP as soon as possible at 709-495-8700 or call 1-800-709-RCMP (7267).

NUMEROUS VEHICLES IMPOUNDED FOLLOWING TRAFFIC STOPS WEDNESDAY NIGHT
(Nov 26)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) seized and impounded numerous vehicles following a series of traffic stops Wednesday night, November 25th.
At 9:25 p.m., officers conducted a traffic stop on Topsail Road, where a 30-year-old man was charged with driving while suspended. The driver also had $3,534 in outstanding fines.
At 9:35 p.m., officers conducted another traffic stop near McDonald’s on Topsail Road, where a 29-year-old man was charged with operating a vehicle without valid insurance.
Just five minutes later, at 9:40 p.m., officers conducted a traffic stop on St. Thomas Line. A 50-year-old man registered a “WARN” on an approved roadside screening device and was issued a seven-day driving suspension. He was also ticketed for failing to transfer vehicle ownership.
At 11:19 p.m., officers conducted a traffic stop near Subway on Hamlyn Road after determining the driver was prohibited from driving anywhere in Canada following an impaired driving conviction.
The man was arrested and charged with driving while prohibited and issued a ticket for driving while suspended. He was transported to the city lockup to await a court appearance.
All vehicles involved in the above incidents were seized and impounded by police

THREE WANTED INDIVIDUALS ARRESTED BY RNC FOLLOWING TWO SEPARATE INCIDENTS
(Nov 26)
The Royal Newfoundland Constabulary (RNC) arrested three individuals on outstanding arrest warrants following two separate incidents on Wednesday, November 25th.
At 4:05 p.m., officers received a complaint of a wanted person in the area of Conways Brook Road. Following an investigation, police located a 30-year-old man and a 28-year-old woman, both of whom were wanted on outstanding arrest warrants.
Both individuals were arrested and charged with failure to appear.
Later that evening, at 7:07 p.m., officers responded to a complaint of unknown trouble at a residence on Bastow Court. Police learned that an intoxicated woman had been at the residence but had since left in a taxi.
Officers later located the 41-year-old woman and arrested her on an outstanding arrest warrant.
All three individuals were transported to the city lockup, where they await their respective court appearances.

WATER OUTAGE AFFECTING ENTIRE TOWN OF HOLYROOD
(Nov 25th)
The Town of Holyrood is advising residents of an emergency water outage affecting the entire town, effective immediately.
In a notice issued by the town, officials say crews are working to address the situation.
Further updates will be provided as more information becomes available.
The town apologizes for the inconvenience and thanks residents for their patience and understanding as crews work to resolve the issue.

TRAFFIC ADVISORY - KENMOUNT ROAD
(Nov 25th)
~ 3:40 p.m; Traffic remains significantly slowed and backed up due to this construction. Expect longer delays as the evening commute starts. 
~ 1:45 p.m; Significant traffic congestion is being seen on Kenmount Road westbound between Pippy Place and Ladysmith Drive in St. John’s. Lane reductions are in place near Kelsey Drive due to ongoing construction, resulting in significant traffic backup.
Please use caution in the area.

GOV NL PUTS PAUSE ON PROPOSED FLAVOURED VAPE RESTRICTIONS
(Nov 25th)
The Government of Newfoundland and Labrador is putting a pause on the proposed changes to the Tobacco and Vapour Products Control Act, which would introduce restrictions on flavoured vaping products.
The decision will allow additional time for public and stakeholder consultations before the government moves forward with the proposed legislation.
The proposed restrictions have not yet been implemented, and no changes are currently in effect.
Further details are expected as the consultation process continues.
